scope.object: the excursion member L^6RLR (its tube's level surface), with m004 as the control and L^10RLR, L^5RLR computed
scope.hypotheses: data-free; exact brute force over det -1 involutions with entries up to 14; the tube identified as the Re-0 fibre by B1847's anti-apex numerics (Re 1/2 to 7e-7); B1846's normalisation of sigma's fixed levels

claim_one_line: THE TUBE'S REAL PART, BY TOPOLOGY (the real number Review 76 owed): sigma's two fixed fibres carry orientation-reversing involutions whose GL(2,Z) class mod 2 decides the reduced Re tau (= I mod 2: Re 0; otherwise Re 1/2 or |tau| = 1); on L^6RLR the two fixed fibres are in opposite classes (exact), and B1847's anti-apex at Re 1/2 (7e-7) is the second, so the tube's level surface has Re tau = 0 exactly -- the metric's own tau at the tube is 0 + 6.15(15) i, differing from the Teichmuller apex (1/2 + 3.65i) in its real part as well as its height; m004 the control (both fixed levels at Re 1/2, as B1847 measured); the even-run pattern observed in four words, not proved. No coupling, scale or ratio; nothing compared with data. 0 of 19.
